title: feat(behaver): verify each experience coordinate marker against the step it cites
description:
## .what
rule.require.experience-coverage (role=behaver) asks a catalog to cite a demo per cell, as a coordinate marker like case=5 [t2]. it does not ask that the citation be verified against the cited step. a marker is a claim about that step given/when, and no glob, count, or type can falsify it.

evidence (one vision, rhachet-roles-bhrain route v2026_09_08.feat-dispute-or-concede-review-budget): three consecutive peer rounds each found mis-cited markers, a driver hand sweep after both lanes approved found two more (a transposed pair), and a fourth round still found three outside the matrix: in a see-also line, in the yield, and in a narrative aside, one of them a [t5] that does not exist in its case.

four shapes:
- over-claim: the step demos no cell; drop the marker (census falls)
- re-file: the step demos a different cell; re-point (census unchanged)
- transpose: two markers cite each other demo; swap (census unchanged)
- dangle: the cited step does not exist; re-point (census unchanged)
three of four move no count, so an arithmetic check cannot find them. and a repair can create one: a step retag left a citation 150 lines away that still named the old cell.

## .why
the census is a sum over markers, so a wrong marker sums identically to a right one. the catalog grows harder to trust as it grows more complete.

## .shape of the fix
1. brief rung: add to the rule that a retag is a rename, and a rename owes a grep of every marker that cites the retagged step
2. half-checker: assert each cited [tn] exists in the cited case file (string match settles the dangle shape)
3. full checker: for every case=N [tn] in the behavior dir (not only the catalog), read the cell coordinates from its position and assert they agree with the cited step given/when plus the case ambient given
